name: Eldercare Locator
description: Free national service that connects older adults and caregivers to local services such as home care, meals, transportation, respite, and caregiver support.
eligibility: Older adults 60+ and their family caregivers

name: VA Caregiver Support Line
description: Phone line staffed by licensed clinical social workers offering support, counseling, and referrals for caregivers of Veterans, and connections to local VA caregiver programs.

name: Alzheimer's Association 24/7 Helpline
description: Around-the-clock helpline with master's-level clinicians for dementia caregivers: information, local resources, crisis and emotional support in more than 200 languages.
eligibility: Anyone affected by Alzheimer's or dementia

name: National Caregiver Help Desk
description: Free help desk giving family caregivers personalized guidance and connections to resources.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Free, confidential 24/7 crisis support by call, text, or chat for anyone in emotional distress or crisis, including overwhelmed caregivers.
eligibility: Anyone in emotional distress or crisis

name: Family Caregiver Alliance
org: Family Caregiver Alliance / National Center on Caregiving
description: Education, resources, and services for family caregivers, including fact sheets, care navigation, and state-by-state resource directories.

name: ARCH National Respite Locator
description: Searchable database to find local respite care providers so caregivers can take a break.

name: 211 (United Way)
description: Free 24/7 helpline connecting people to local help with bills, food, housing, and caregiving resources; call or text 211.

name: National Family Caregiver Support Program
description: Federally funded program delivered through Area Agencies on Aging providing information, respite, counseling, and training to family caregivers; access via your local agency or the Eldercare Locator.
eligibility: Caregivers of adults 60+, caregivers of any-age individuals with dementia, or relatives 55+ raising children

name: AARP Family Caregiving Resource Line
description: Toll-free line offering information, guidance, and support for family caregivers, plus online tools and guides.
eligibility: Family and informal caregivers (no membership required)

name: Well Spouse Association
description: Peer support for spouses and partners caring for a chronically ill or disabled loved one, including support groups and a newsletter.
eligibility: Spouses and partners who are caregivers

name: PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly)
description: Program that coordinates and pays for medical and social services so older adults needing nursing-home-level care can stay in the community, easing the caregiving load.
eligibility: Adults 55+ with Medicare and/or Medicaid who need nursing-home-level care
